note: Stage 2d (22 Nov 2026, docs/design/ANIMAL_ROUTINES_TRAILS_TRAPPING.md, TR-13): signs along the trails, worked out on each client from the routes it already has (same spots for every player, no server cost). Rabbits leave pellet latrines by the warren and at the grazing end of a run and dig scrapes where runs of different warrens meet; deer leave prints where a trail crosses wet ground and droppings by the bed (Ziege et al. 2016, BMC Ecology, rabbit latrines; onX and Idaho Fish and Game on deer sign). A player sees them from Tracking skill see_level (latrines and droppings) and fine_level (scrapes and prints; both 0 since Dave's 23 Nov 2026 ruling that signs are simply there for everyone, see everyone_note; they were 5 and 25), within draw_m (min at see_level, max at 100). Nothing is made before the player has ground (the first-join window). Provisional.
ground_note: Lane A 23 Nov: no sign was drawn while standing still. A sign whose ground has no collision yet is worked out again every ground_retry_s, at most ground_retries times before the player moves.
size_note: Lane A 23 Nov: pellets, mounds and the faint halo were not seen at standing height. pellet_scale and mound_scale make them larger than true size (pellets 3x, mounds 1.3 to 1.8x) so a heap and a warren read at a glance.
patch_note: Lane A 23 Nov: the latrines lay in knee-high grass. The grass round a latrine, droppings and a warren is pressed short and pale (grass_view run map), patch_m the radius; Pellets lie 6 cm up, over the leaf cards (3 cm), on a darker scratched patch; the glow is warm gold (pale vanished on the pale pressed ground). glow_emit and halo_emit give the spot glow and the Tracking halo a little light of their own so they show on litter and in shade.
spot_note: Spotting (Dave 23 Nov 2026: 'spotting animal markings should highlight the markings, make a slight sound and give xp for finding them'): a shown sign the player first comes within spot_m of glows for glow_s (a soft pale patch, glow_color, up to glow_alpha), the sound sign_spot plays there when sound_with allows it (batch3_slots.json; see sound_note) and the server trains Tracking once per sign (traps.json tracking sign_*); one sign every spot_gap_s, so each of a cluster is trained (the practice cooldown is 2 s).
sound_note: Dave 25 Nov 2026 (QA #20, R-HUNT-SIGN-SOUND): 'I think the sounds to indicate animal signs is intrusive and needs to be much more subtle but also it shouldn't always sound. maybe only when we have a hunting weapon in our hand or a snare or trap maybe.' The spot sound plays only while one of sound_with is in either hand (spears, bows, crossbows, the sling, clubs, snares and bird traps; not the fishing spear or the fish trap), at sign_spot's play_db (batch3_slots.json, 12 dB under before). The glow and the Tracking XP are unchanged.
everyone_note: Dave 23 Nov 2026: 'signs should just be there and if you have a higher tracking skill maybe they get highlighted or glow a little'. Every kind of sign shows to everyone from the first level (see_level and fine_level 0); Tracking only reaches farther (draw_m, 15 m untrained to 30 m at 100) and, from halo_from, lays a faint steady pale patch under each shown sign within halo_reach_m (halo_alpha from halo_from to 100, lit like the ground with a faint light of its own, halo_emit, so it shows faintly at night: the eye catching it, not a marker). The spot glow and XP stay as they were; the sound follows sound_note. Provisional.
halo_note: Dave 23 Nov 2026 (docs/RULINGS.md R-HUNT-GLOW): once you train to 25 "you will start seeing some animal signs glowing at a close distance say 10 meters even further at higher levels". The halo starts at halo_from 25, on signs within halo_reach_m[0] (10 m) there, rising to halo_reach_m[1] at 100 (never past the signs' own draw_m reach).
latrine_note: Lane A 23 Nov 2026 (Job S): 8 to 15 pellets of 1.6 cm at ground level under leaf litter and grass did not show at all. A latrine is now 30 to 50 pellets of about 2 cm on a dark scratched-earth patch about 0.65 m across (real rabbit latrines hold dozens to hundreds of pellets, often on a scraped patch), lifted 6 cm over the leaf cards (3.5 cm for deer droppings); deer droppings 15 to 25.
hop_note: Rabbit prints in mud (23 Nov 2026, hunting thread): where a rabbit run crosses wet ground, hop_sets hops hop_step_m apart, each the two long hind feet side by side ahead and the two small fore feet behind (the classic rabbit track; Idaho Fish and Game track guide), one line per prints_every_m like the deer prints.
warren_note: Warrens drawn for everyone (Dave 23 Nov 2026: 'so rabbit warrens actually have a model or image'): at every warren home, from the routes the client already has, warren_holes mounds of dug earth with a hole (burrow_view.gd's mound) within warren_m of the home, the holes facing out. Live rabbits' own burrows are still drawn by burrow_view from the server. Provisional.
bed_note: Deer beds (23 Nov 2026, hunting thread; Dave: 'extrapolate from them and see what would make for a fun hunting game'): deer lie up by day in small groups, each leaving an oval of pressed grass or leaves about its body's size, the plainest sign that a trail's end is a bedding place (Penn State Extension and onX on deer beds). bed_count beds within bed_off_m of each deer trail's home; grass_view presses the grass in bed_size_m ovals (the worn-earth ground bares the litter there), so no mesh. Provisional.
rub_note: Rubbed trees (23 Nov 2026, hunting thread): stags (and elk, moose) rub the bark off saplings and small trunks along their trails and near beds, a pale strip at knee to chest height that shows from far off (onX 'How to read deer sign'; Texas Parks and Wildlife hunter education). Along each deer trail at most one every rub_every_m (after a stretch with no thin trunk, looked for again rub_retry_m on), the thinnest loaded trunk up to rub_max_r_m within rub_m of the trail; the strip rub_height_m up its trail side. Provisional.
read_note: Reading a sign (23 Nov 2026, hunting thread): look right at a sign (within about 10 degrees of the reticle, read_aim_cos) within read_m and press E; a looser look leaves E to the item, snare or plant nearby. Anyone reads what it is and who left it (Dave: signs are there for everyone); from read_way_level (the Tracking the Map shows trails at, Dave's 10) which way the trail runs from it and to what; from read_habit_level (Advanced, Dave's skill classes) when the animal uses it, from the routines (rabbits out from about sunset to sunrise, deer feed at dusk and bed by day). Texts after Sal's animal_sign.json hints. Provisional.

latrine.what: A heap of small round pellets on scratched earth. Rabbits mark their run here.
latrine.habit: Rabbits come out along it from about sunset and are back underground after sunrise.

scrape.what: A shallow scrape where two rabbit runs meet.
scrape.habit: Rabbits from two warrens cross here at night: a good place for a snare.

prints.what: Split hoof prints pressed in the soft ground. Deer passed here.
prints.habit: Deer walk this way to feed at dusk and back to their beds at dawn.

droppings.what: A pile of dark pellets. Deer lie up close by.
droppings.habit: Deer bed near here through the day.

bed.what: An oval of pressed-down grass. A deer lay here.
bed.habit: Deer lie here by day and leave at dusk: come quietly, downwind.

warren.what: Mounds of dug earth with dark holes. A rabbit warren.
warren.habit: By day the rabbits keep below; they come out along their runs from about sunset.

hops.what: Small prints in the mud, two long ones ahead of two small ones. A rabbit hopped through.
hops.habit: Rabbits come along this run from about sunset to sunrise.

rub.what: Bark rubbed off a young tree. A stag marked his trail.
rub.habit: Stags walk this trail between the beds and the feeding ground.
